Measured result: Same-script/different-language direct retrieval (7.53%) exceeds same-language/different-script direct retrieval (5.36%).
Implementation guidance: Do not use raw embedding proximity or shared tokenizer/script identity as the sole language-sharing criterion. Treat script as an explicit surface coordinate.
Concrete engineering test: For every candidate shared expert, report same-script surface controls before interpreting representation overlap.

Measured result: Same-language script swaps gain +4.25 pp after matched transfer; permuted alignment returns to ~0.51% chance.
Implementation guidance: Use transfer-over-direct gain as a stronger pre-routing signal than absolute surface similarity.
Concrete engineering test: Require a true matched-semantic held-out gain above the direct baseline and a permuted-alignment control before promoting a compatibility edge.

Measured result: Script-neutral same-language retrieval reaches 28.78% direct and 33.53% mapped.
Implementation guidance: Provide a script-normalized or relation-oriented pathway alongside glyph-specific lexical pathways. Shared trunks can operate on script-neutral structure while surface adapters retain orthographic detail.
Concrete engineering test: Ablate glyph identity or transliterate/normalize in a controlled branch and measure whether task/meaning neighbourhoods are preserved.

Measured result: Surface script displacement stable rank 14.96; neutral residual 4.39.
Implementation guidance: Do not force script conversion into one tiny global adapter at the raw token surface. Allocate enough surface capacity, then compress after script-specific recoding has been resolved.
Concrete engineering test: Measure displacement spectra before choosing adapter rank; compare raw-script and script-neutral residual ranks.

Measured result: PCA-4D retains 20.80% and PCA-8D 31.35% of 10-NN structure.
Implementation guidance: Keep local-control bottlenecks separate from whole-sentence representation capacity. The 2-3 local movement result should not be reused as a whole-sentence latent-size prescription.
Concrete engineering test: Evaluate neighbourhood preservation whenever a multilingual bottleneck is reduced; reject dimensions that destroy the sentence-level neighbourhood needed by the task.

Implementation guidance: Treat script compatibility as distribution-conditioned. A script adapter that works on shuffled meanings still needs a topic/contiguous holdout.
Concrete engineering test: Include blocked/topic holdout in multilingual sharing regressions and store the random-to-blocked degradation.

Measured result: Script pairs are heterogeneous: Tamasheq/Minangkabau strong, Chinese negative raw transfer gain.
Implementation guidance: Route by measured relation, not by a binary “same language” flag. Some script pairs can share a lightweight recoder; others may require richer language-specific realization layers.
Concrete engineering test: Maintain pair-level compatibility records and allow asymmetric adapter capacity rather than one universal script-conversion module.
